contract: Pure readiness and cycle admission Elzoo.DependencyGraph over caller Work Item fixtures, externals, typed edges (from waits for to) and provenance-tagged facts with explicit Unix-ms now: closed is not completed, unknown/expired/model-declared-only facts never satisfy, blocking-edge admission revalidates the whole graph; the Cure step keeps the index-level blocking graph acyclic (Cure laws) while the Elixir revalidation and mapping are test-grounded; exact issues, blockers and errors.
limits: Selected laws cover the Cure decisions only; the Elixir validation, ID-to-index mapping, duplicate/unknown/unplaceable flags, blocker reasons, contradictions, cycle path and commit mapping are test-grounded.
Laws are scoped over the Bool results of builtin Int equality and order; their integer meaning is an upstream Cure contract plus boundary tests.
Only the safe direction is proved: admitted implies acyclic. Search completeness (admitted iff unreachable) is a finite test; a defective search returns {:error, :search_disagreement}.
No execution, claiming, lease, scheduling, notification, durable storage or distributed admission; the serialized owner is a test double under test/ (runtime/unit is a test-only dependency).
No join/fan-in policy beyond every blocking prerequisite satisfied; skip/fail handling of a prerequisite is the caller's.

Bounds: 1000 nodes, 10000 edges (the proposal counts), 10000 facts; no performance claim. One laptop observation: readiness at full bounds took about 6.7 s, so it must not run inside a default-timeout GenServer.call such as Elzoo.Unit.step/2 (5000 ms); one admission took about 0.2 s.

grounding.claim: Law 1 (#43 'unknown never satisfies'): list induction over the full fact list; if every fact is for another target, unknown, unsatisfied, model-declared or expired, the actual fact_support equals false. Scoped over the Bool results of builtin Int equality and order.
Law 2: an undeclared target (lookup None) never satisfies, by reduction.
Law 2: a duplicate target never satisfies, whatever its lifecycle or support, by reduction.
Law 2: an unplaceable target never satisfies, whatever its lifecycle or support, by reduction.
Law 2: a unique, placeable completed target satisfies for any support, by reduction.
Law 2: a unique, placeable cancelled target never satisfies for any support, by reduction.
Law 2: a unique, placeable closed-without-completion target never satisfies for any support, by reduction.
Law 2: a unique, placeable open item target is satisfied exactly by fact support, by reduction.
Law 2: a unique, placeable external target is satisfied exactly by fact support, by reduction.
Law 2: a single unknown fact never attributes, for every provenance, expiry and now.
Law 2: a single unsatisfied fact never attributes, for every provenance, expiry and now.
Law 2: a single model-declared fact never attributes, for every value, expiry and now.
Law 2: a fact whose builtin now < expiry result is false never attributes (scoped over that Bool result).
Law 3: an informational edge leaves item_ready unchanged (kind is tested before the endpoint), by reduction.
Law 3: a hierarchy edge leaves item_ready unchanged, by reduction.
Law 4: induction over the full edge list; one blocking edge from i (builtin from == i evidence) to an unsatisfied target makes item_ready equal false, for every lifecycle and flag.
Law 4: an open item whose builtin now < deferred_until result is true is never ready.
Law 4: a flagged duplicate item is never ready, by reduction.
Law 4: a flagged unplaceable item is never ready, by reduction.
Law 4: a non-open (completed) item is never ready, by reduction.

Law 5 (equality form): for every edge list, endpoints and candidate set s accepted by the closure certificate, a cycle (inductive DgCycle/DgWalk relation) through E(x, m) in the graph with the new edge prepended, plus a refutation of such a cycle in the old graph, proves True = False; the search is untrusted.

Law 5 over the committed state (equality form): when the Cure admission_step admits a blocking proposal, a cycle of blocking(next) through E(x, m) plus a refutation of such a cycle in blocking(es) proves True = False.
Law 5a: blocking([RE(blocking, f, t) | es]) reduces to [E(f, t) | blocking(es)].
Law 5a: blocking([RE(informational, f, t) | es]) reduces to blocking(es).
Law 5a: blocking([RE(hierarchy, f, t) | es]) reduces to blocking(es).
Law 5a: an admitted informational proposal leaves blocking(next) equal to blocking(es).
Law 5a: an admitted hierarchy proposal leaves blocking(next) equal to blocking(es).
Law 6: a blocking proposal whose admits result is false leaves the Cure admission_step state unchanged.
Pinned Cure checks every declaration with @total true, including core/operator's Transition; the Cure audit reports no axioms, holes, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or not-proven-total entries.

Law audit, @total presence, 16 negative controls rejected by the kernel, :erlang-only BEAM imports; listed readiness, fact, expiry/deferral boundary, closed-vs-completed, model-declared, contradiction, issue-kind, bound/error, admission precedence and path scenarios; exhaustive admission comparison on small graphs and random larger graphs; serialized Elzoo.Unit race and snapshot-then-commit negative control. Finite evidence, not proofs.
Relies on pinned Cure kernel, totality checking, compilation and runtime semantics, including the integer meaning of builtin Int equality and order; not a local soundness proof.
Elixir validation and execution of the shell are upstream contracts.
OTP 29.1.2 GenServer call serialization in the test-only Elzoo.Unit owner is an upstream contract; no durable or distributed admission.
Callers supply truthful lifecycle tags, provenance, sources, expiries and a now translated from their clock; provenance is not authenticated here.

telemetry.contract: Pure decision; no execution to observe. A shipped owner would require re-declaration.

config.contract: No settings: order, deferral, expiry and now are per-call data; bounds are fixed Contract constants.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; the serialized owner is the caller's (test double under test/ only).
